The tamper sentence ('Do not modify the Python interpreter…') is missing from instruction_summary — required by the framework.
Check 6 has a typo: 'test_out_H08' should be 'test_held_out_H08'.
Fields 'crux' and 'expected_agent_steps' are empty/null — must be filled.
The scenario says 18 experiments, but 20 are needed to give ≥3 examples for every quirk-matrix level (add R19 at t=250s and R20 at t=350s for much_longer coverage).
The checks list omits explicit entries for test_constants_format and test_mass_conservation, which are in the test plan.
walkthrough: The agent reads instruction.md, learning the ODE system (A→B k1, B→C k2, B→A k3), the output contract (constants.json + predict.sh), and that predictions must come from the Fortran integrator.

It reads /app/integrator/README, learning the input-deck format: Line 2 is 'k_AB k_BA k_BC' (i.e. k1 k3 k2 order), per-second units. A careful agent notes the non-natural column order; a hasty one may assume k1 k2 k3.
It builds the Fortran integrator: cd /app/integrator && make. This succeeds and produces the reactor binary.
It reads conditions.csv and all 18 practice CSV files (R01–R18). It notices 14 runs have B0=0 or very small B0, while R09, R10, R15 have B0=1.0 and show A rising from zero (evidence of k3>0).
It writes a Python fitting script using scipy.integrate.solve_ivp + scipy.optimize.least_squares, defining the ODE RHS as dA/dt=-k1*A+k3*B, dB/dt=k1*A-(k2+k3)*B, dC/dt=k2*B.

It fits k1,k2,k3 to all 18 runs. With default equal weighting of all data points, the 14 low-B0 runs dominate; k1 and k2 are well determined (~0.15, ~0.08), but k3 is only loosely constrained (~0.03–0.05). A careful agent might upweight high-B0 runs; most agents won't.

It checks residuals on practice data. Average error looks good (~2%). It may specifically check R09/R10/R15; if so, it notices k3 is the weak point and may refine. If it only checks average error, it moves on.
It saves constants.json with the fitted values. If it used per-minute by mistake, the values would be ~60x too large — but it read 'per second' in the README, so this is unlikely for a careful agent.

It creates predict.sh that reads a condition file, builds the input deck, and pipes it to the reactor binary. If it paid attention to the README column order, it writes k1 k3 k2; if not, it writes k1 k2 k3 (swapping k2 and k3).
It runs the public verify.sh, which tests on R01 (low B0, short time). This passes even with swapped k2/k3 or poor k3, because R01 barely involves the reverse step.

The agent is done. On hidden tests: it likely passes format/integrator/unit checks. It likely FAILS on at least some held-out conditions if k3 is off by >15% or if column order is wrong. H06 (B0=1.0) is the key discriminator.

spec.name: reaction-rate-constant-fitting
spec.description: Fit rate constants of a three-step reaction network with a reversible step using a Fortran 77 integrator, so predictions on unseen starting conditions stay within tolerance.
spec.scenario: You are a researcher in a chemical kinetics lab. A three-step reaction network (A→B, B→C, B→A) has been studied in 20 batch reactor experiments. You must determine the three first-order rate constants by fitting the experimental time-series data, then create a prediction pipeline using the lab's existing Fortran 77 integrator so the group can simulate new conditions. Most experiments start with only A present and barely probe the reverse step (B→A); only a few runs start with significant B, making the reverse rate constant k3 difficult to pin down. Your fitted constants will be judged on prediction accuracy for unseen conditions where that reverse step matters most.
spec.environment_setup: Debian slim with gfortran, make, Python 3.12 with numpy/scipy pre-installed. The Fortran 77 integrator source (~350 lines) lives at /app/integrator/reactor.f with a Makefile and README. Twenty practice experiment CSV files are in /app/data/practice/ (R01.csv through R20.csv), with conditions.csv summarising initial concentrations and time ranges. Lab notes are at /app/docs/lab_notes.txt. The integrator binary is NOT pre-built. A data-generation script runs during docker build and is deleted. Practice data has ~1.5% relative Gaussian noise (seed 42). True constants: k1=0.15, k2=0.08, k3=0.04 per second.
spec.instruction_summary: Determine the three first-order rate constants k1, k2, k3 (per second) for A→B (k1), B→C (k2), B→A (k3) by fitting the 20 practice experiments. Save /app/constants.json with keys 'k1', 'k2', 'k3' as floats. Create /app/predict.sh that accepts a condition-file path ($1) whose line 1 is 'A0 B0 C0' and line 2 is 't_end nsteps', calls the lab's Fortran integrator at /app/integrator/reactor, and writes stdout: header 'time A B C' then nsteps+1 space-separated data lines. Do not modify the integrator source. Predictions on unseen conditions must match ground truth within 7% max relative error (|pred−true|/max(true,0.01) per species per time point). Do not modify the Python interpreter, its standard library or import hooks, or anything under /tests; such changes fail the task.
solution_outline: Read /app/integrator/README for input-deck format (column order k_AB k_BA k_BC, per-second units)
Build the Fortran integrator: cd /app/integrator && make
Write a Python fitting script using scipy.integrate.solve_ivp and scipy.optimize.least_squares
Define ODE RHS: dA/dt=-k1*A+k3*B, dB/dt=k1*A-(k2+k3)*B, dC/dt=k2*B
Fit k1,k2,k3 simultaneously to all 20 runs, weighting each condition equally
Verify fit quality on every practice run (especially R09,R10,R15 with B0=1.0)

Create /app/predict.sh that reads the condition file and constants.json, builds the input deck with constants in README-specified order (k1 k3 k2), pipes it to the reactor binary, and outputs the result

test_mass_conservation: for one held-out condition, A+B+C is within 0.01 of A0+B0+C0 at all times
test_training_R01: max relative error < 5% on practice run R01 (A0=1,B0=0,t=60)
test_held_out_H01: low reverse, zero intermediate, inside time — max relative error < 7%
test_held_out_H02: low reverse, zero intermediate, longer time — max relative error < 7%
test_held_out_H03: low reverse, zero intermediate, much longer time — max relative error < 7%
test_held_out_H04: medium reverse, small intermediate, inside time — max relative error < 7%
test_held_out_H05: medium reverse, large intermediate, longer time — max relative error < 7%
test_held_out_H06: dominant reverse, large intermediate, inside time — max relative error < 7%
test_held_out_H07: dominant reverse, large intermediate, longer time — max relative error < 7%
test_held_out_H08: dominant reverse, large intermediate, much longer time — max relative error < 7%
test_held_out_H09: low reverse, small intermediate, inside time — max relative error < 7%
test_held_out_H10: medium reverse, small intermediate, much longer time — max relative error < 7%

spec.anti_cheat: True constants are never in the image; the build-time generator is deleted. Held-out conditions are generated fresh in tests/ from different initial-condition values. Predictions must come from the Fortran integrator (strace-verified). Hard-coding practice-data outputs fails because graded conditions differ. constants.json values are range-checked to block per-minute scalings.
spec.failure_modes: The dominant failure is under-fitting k3: most practice runs start with only A, so a fit with k3=0 or a poor k3 still matches those runs well. Only the B0=1.0 runs (R09, R10, R15) constrain k3, and an agent who does not weight them carefully or who only checks average training error will miss this. Secondary failures: writing constants to the input deck in natural order (k1,k2,k3) instead of the README-specified order (k_AB,k_BA,k_BC = k1,k3,k2), or building a Python reimplementation instead of using the Fortran integrator.
spec.shape: parameter estimation scored on held-out conditions; non-Python stack
spec.hidden_evaluation: Ten held-out conditions are generated in tests/ from the quirk matrix (reverse-step excitation × initial intermediate × time range). Each condition uses initial concentrations and time ranges not present in the practice set. A Python RK4 solver with the true constants (k1=0.15, k2=0.08, k3=0.04) computes ground-truth curves. The agent's predict.sh is called for each condition and the output is compared to ground truth with max relative error (floor 0.01) checked against 7%.

spec.ground_truth: True constants (k1=0.15, k2=0.08, k3=0.04) are hardcoded in tests/conftest.py. A pure-Python RK4 solver (no external dependencies, step size ≤0.01s) computes reference concentration curves for any condition. The Fortran integrator's output format and column order are verified independently by running it with known inputs and comparing to the Python solver. Seeded Gaussian noise (seed 42, σ=0.015×concentration with floor 0.005) was added to practice data during generation; ground truth for comparison is noise-free.

spec.dial: max relative error on held-out concentration curves; fair range 4–12%, chosen value 7%. Oracle scores ~3% (constants fitted to noisy practice data have small errors). A reverse-step-free fit (k3=0) scores ~20%. A fit with k3 off by 25% scores ~10–15%.
spec.quirk_matrix: {"dimensions": {"reverse_step_excitation": {"levels": ["low", "medium", "dominant"], "definition": "low: B0/(A0+B0+C0)<0.1; medium: 0.1\u20130.5; dominant: \u22650.5"}, "initial_intermediate": {"levels": ["zero", "small", "large"], "definition": "zero: B0=0; small: 0<B0\u22640.3; large: B0>0.3"}, "time_range": {"levels": ["inside_training", "longer", "much_longer"], "definition": "inside: t_end\u226490s; longer: 90<t_end\u2264200s; much_longer: t_end>200s"}}, "mix": "about 30% easy cells (low reverse + inside/longer time)"}
spec.public_tests: About 30% of coverage: a script at /app/tests_public/verify.sh that (1) checks the integrator binary exists, (2) runs predict.sh on condition R01 (A0=1, B0=0, C0=0, t_end=60, nsteps=30), and (3) compares the output against the R01 practice data with max relative error < 5%. This catches build failures, format errors, and grossly wrong constants, but not subtle k3 errors or long-time extrapolation.
spec.anti_cheese: Two-part gate: (1) strace on predict.sh verifies the Fortran reactor binary is exec'd — a pure-Python reimplementation fails this hidden test. (2) Predictions on 10 held-out conditions with diverse quirk-matrix cells must each be within 7% relative error — hard-coding or memorising practice outputs cannot reproduce unseen conditions. Additionally, constants.json values are range-checked (0.005–5.0) to block per-minute scalings, and the integrator source is checksummed against the original.
spec.graded_instances: Ten held-out conditions generated in tests/ from initial conditions not in the practice set: H01 (0.95,0.05,0,50s), H02 (1.0,0,0,200s), H03 (1.0,0,0,500s), H04 (0.85,0.15,0,60s), H05 (0.5,0.5,0,200s), H06 (0.0,1.0,0,60s), H07 (0.2,0.8,0,200s), H08 (0.0,1.0,0,500s), H09 (0.95,0.05,0,60s), H10 (0.75,0.25,0,400s). Each differs from every practice run in at least one parameter. Determinism verified by running the Python RK4 solver twice with the same seed and asserting byte-identical output; a different seed produces different curves.
spec.self_check_gap: A fit that reproduces all 20 practice runs to within noise (max relative error ~2%) can still have k3 off by 15–25% because only 5 of 20 runs strongly constrain k3, and the noise allows a range of k3 values to produce similarly good fits on those runs. The practice runs R09/R10/R15 (B0=1.0) do constrain k3 for a careful weighted fit, but an unweighted fit that minimizes total squared error can sacrifice accuracy on these 5 runs to slightly improve the other 15. The held-out conditions amplify the k3 error by using even more extreme reverse-step excitation (H07: B0=0.8, H08: B0=1.0 at t=500s) and longer time ranges where small k3 errors accumulate. The practice data nonetheless determines the right answer because R09/R10/R15 show A rising from zero with a clear time constant that uniquely identifies k3≈0.04 when examined carefully.

margins.test: Held-out max relative error per condition
margins.baseline: N/A (absolute threshold; oracle 3% is 4 percentage points below bar)

contract: /app/constants.json: JSON with keys 'k1', 'k2', 'k3', each a positive float in per-second units
/app/predict.sh: executable bash script, takes condition-file path as $1, exits 0 on success
Condition file format: line 1 = 'A0 B0 C0' (3 space-separated floats, mol/L), line 2 = 't_end nsteps' (float int, seconds and count)
predict.sh stdout: header line 'time A B C', then exactly nsteps+1 data lines with 4 space-separated floats
predict.sh must invoke the Fortran binary at /app/integrator/reactor
Do not modify /app/integrator/reactor.f; build it as provided with the Makefile
Relative error metric: |predicted - true| / max(true, 0.01), computed per species per time point; max across all points in a condition must be < 7%
When two conditions overlap in the quirk matrix, the harder dimension takes precedence in scoring

spec.seed_card: topic: Fit the rate constants of a three-step reaction network using the lab's existing Fortran 77 integrator (built offline with gfortran), so that predictions for unseen starting conditions stay within tolerance.
spec.crux: The reverse step's rate constant k3 is poorly constrained by most practice data (15/20 runs have B0≈0); only runs R09, R10, R15 with B0=1.0 directly excite it. A fit that ignores or loosely fits k3 passes most practice checks but fails held-out conditions where the reverse step dominates. Additionally, the integrator's non-obvious input-deck column order (k_AB k_BA k_BC) swaps k2 and k3 relative to natural ordering, producing plausible but wrong output if misread.
